entries.name: IMAP_HOST
entries.description: The host name of the mailbox's IMAP server, which the connector reaches over implicit TLS (IMAP over TLS, port 993 unless IMAP_PORT says otherwise). Just the name: no imaps://, no port and no path. The server's certificate must be valid for this name.
howToGet: Find the incoming mail (IMAP) server in the mail provider's settings for mail apps; it usually starts imap.
Use the server for IMAP over TLS (SSL/TLS, usually port 993). The connector doesn't use STARTTLS (port 143) or plaintext.

entries.name: IMAP_PORT
entries.description: The IMAP server's port for implicit TLS. Leave it empty for 993, the usual port; set it only if the provider gives another TLS port.
howToGet: Leave empty for 993. A port the provider names for STARTTLS (usually 143) won't work: the connector only speaks TLS from the first byte.

entries.name: IMAP_USERNAME
entries.description: The mailbox's sign-in name for IMAP, usually its full address. One mailbox per instance. Not a secret, but it names the mailbox.
howToGet: Use the name the provider's mail-app settings give for IMAP; for most it is the mailbox's address.

entries.name: IMAP_PASSWORD
entries.description: An app password for the mailbox, sent only to the IMAP server with LOGIN inside the TLS connection. The connector only opens folders read-only and never changes, moves or deletes mail, but IMAP passwords aren't scoped, so this one could: keep it to the host's secret store, and revoke it when the connector is turned off.
howToGet: In the mailbox's security settings, create an app password (some providers call it an app-specific or device password) named KaratOS. Most providers ask for one once two-step sign-in is on, and won't take the account's own password over IMAP.
Make sure IMAP access is turned on for the mailbox, if the provider has a switch for it.
Copy the app password straight into the host's secret store. Never paste it into chat or an issue.
